scenes.tts: Take the calcium away, and this sheet of cells comes apart. What was the calcium holding together? Put it back, and the cells knit together again.
scenes.narration: Take the calcium away, and this sheet of cells comes apart. What was the calcium holding together? Put it back, and the cells knit together again.
scenes.caption: Take the calcium away, and this sheet of cells comes apart. What was the calcium holding together? Put it back, and the cells knit together again.
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film: a side-on cross-section of an epithelium filling about 70% of frame height. A row of four tall GREY cells with nuclei stands side by side, touching; under them a thin flat ORANGE sheet (the basement membrane); below that a loose bed of wavy ORANGE ropes in a pale orange haze (the matrix). Fluid above the cells is dotted with drifting YELLOW calcium dots, gently moving all the time. Label top-left: 'a sheet of epithelial cells'. On 'Take the calcium away' the yellow dots drain out of the frame upward; the cells shrink and round up, gaps open between them, and they pull away from each other. On 'What was the calcium holding together?' the question appears across the top in white and stays. On 'Put it back' the yellow dots stream back in, the cells spread and close the gaps until the row is whole again. COLOUR MAP for the whole film (one colour per concept, same in the lesson's take-homes): YELLOW = calcium (small dots); BLUE = cadherin (the outer arms); PURPLE = integrin (two lobes, alpha and beta); TEAL = adaptor proteins inside the cell (catenins, talin, vinculin, desmoplakin, plectin); GREEN = actin cable; PINK = keratin cable; ORANGE = the matrix (collagen ropes, fibronectin, the RGD tag, the basement membrane sheet, the proteoglycan gel tinted pale orange); GOLD = pull (a travelling gold pulse along a chain, gold arrows); GREY = cell outlines, membranes and nuclei; labels in TEXT white or the concept colour, size 28 or more.
Title 'One Chain, Four Links' fades in over the top of the world for 2 s while the yellow dots keep drifting; the hook question fades out under it.

scenes.tts: Each cell reaches across with arms called cadherins. Calcium sits at the joints of each arm and keeps it stiff. The arm on one cell grips the arm on the next.
scenes.narration: Each cell reaches across with arms called cadherins. Calcium sits at the joints of each arm and keeps it stiff. The arm on one cell grips the arm on the next.
scenes.caption: Each cell reaches across with arms called cadherins. Calcium sits at the joints of each arm and keeps it stiff. The arm on one cell grips the arm on the next.
scenes.visual: Already zooming as the scene starts: the camera moves smoothly into the narrow gap between the two middle cells until the two membranes are vertical GREY bands filling the frame height. Show first, then name: from each membrane, BLUE beaded rods (five beads each, a row of three per membrane) extend into the gap. YELLOW dots settle into the joints between beads, and each rod straightens as its joints fill. On 'grips', the tips of opposing rods from the two cells meet and interlock in the middle of the gap with a small flash. Label 'cadherin' in BLUE beside one rod. The yellow dots in the gap keep jiggling slightly.

scenes.tts: Follow one arm into the cell. Adaptor proteins grip its tail and pass the hold inward: beta-catenin, then alpha-catenin. They tie it to a cable, a filament of actin. This grip is an adherens junction.
scenes.narration: Follow one arm into the cell. Adaptor proteins grip its tail and pass the hold inward: β-catenin, then α-catenin. They tie it to a cable, a filament of actin. This grip is an adherens junction.
scenes.caption: Follow one arm into the cell. Adaptor proteins grip its tail and pass the hold inward: β-catenin, then α-catenin. They tie it to a cable, a filament of actin. This grip is an adherens junction.
scenes.visual: Camera pans left into the left cell, keeping the gap at the right edge. The BLUE cadherin's tail continues through the membrane into the cell. On 'beta-catenin', a TEAL rounded block snaps onto the tail; on 'alpha-catenin', a second TEAL block snaps onto the first. On 'a filament of actin', a long GREEN cable grows from the left edge of the cell toward the TEAL blocks and docks onto the alpha-catenin block. Labels appear as each part docks: 'β-catenin', 'α-catenin' (TEAL), 'actin cable' (GREEN). Mirror the same chain in the right cell, fading in more quickly. On 'adherens junction', a white bracket spans both cells' chains with the label 'adherens junction'. Labelled blocks only: no molecular structures.

scenes.tts: So, in its simplest form, one grip is a chain of four links. A partner outside, a receptor in the membrane, adaptors, and a cable inside.
scenes.narration: So, in its simplest form, one grip is a chain of four links. A partner outside, a receptor in the membrane, adaptors, and a cable inside.
scenes.caption: So, in its simplest form, one grip is a chain of four links. A partner outside, a receptor in the membrane, adaptors, and a cable inside.
scenes.visual: Zoom out slightly so the left cell's full chain runs horizontally across the frame: GREEN actin cable, TEAL adaptors, BLUE cadherin crossing the membrane, the neighbour's BLUE cadherin beyond. A small white corner label 'simplest form' appears; four numbered white tags pop up one after another as the narrator names them, each under its link: '1 partner outside' under the neighbour's cadherin, '2 receptor' under this cell's cadherin, '3 adaptors' under the TEAL blocks, '4 cable' under the GREEN actin. Each link briefly brightens as its tag appears. Yellow calcium dots keep drifting in the gap.

scenes.tts: Now pull on the sheet. In this simple picture, the pull runs from cable to cable, through every link. Break any one link, and this path is cut.
scenes.narration: Now pull on the sheet. In this simple picture, the pull runs from cable to cable, through every link. Break any one link, and this path is cut.
scenes.caption: Now pull on the sheet. In this simple picture, the pull runs from cable to cable, through every link. Break any one link, and this path is cut.
scenes.visual: Two GOLD arrows appear at the far left and far right edges, pointing outward, and the two cells stretch slightly apart. A bright GOLD pulse travels along the chain from the left cell's GREEN cable, through the TEAL adaptors, both BLUE cadherins and the neighbour's TEAL adaptors, into the neighbour's GREEN cable; then it repeats (corner label 'one simple chain, schematic'). No gauges. On 'Break any one link', one link briefly flickers out in grey and the GOLD pulse stops at it, then the link returns and the pulse resumes; the white text 'one break cuts the path' appears at the top and stays.

scenes.tts: Now take the calcium away. Which link gives way first? The arms outside, the adaptors, or the cable? Choose one.
scenes.narration: Now take the calcium away. Which link gives way first? The arms outside, the adaptors, or the cable? Choose one.
scenes.caption: Now take the calcium away. Which link gives way first? The arms outside, the adaptors, or the cable? Choose one.
scenes.visual: The GOLD pull arrows stay on, the gauges fade. The question card appears at the top in white: 'No calcium: which link fails first?' Three white outline boxes, labelled 'arms outside', 'adaptors' and 'cable', highlight the BLUE cadherins, the TEAL blocks and the GREEN actin in turn, one on each option as it is spoken. The yellow dots in the gap begin to dim but have not yet left.

Thinking pause. The question card and the three outline boxes stay on screen, all three boxes softly pulsing together. The chain is held under gentle pull: the GOLD arrows breathe slightly; nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Calcium leaves the joints, and the arms go floppy. The outer link lets go. The adaptors and the cable are still there, but this contact can no longer pass the pull across. One broken link, and the sheet comes apart.
scenes.narration: Calcium leaves the joints, and the arms go floppy. The outer link lets go. The adaptors and the cable are still there, but this contact can no longer pass the pull across. One broken link, and the sheet comes apart.
scenes.caption: Calcium leaves the joints, and the arms go floppy. The outer link lets go. The adaptors and the cable are still there, but this contact can no longer pass the pull across. One broken link, and the sheet comes apart.
scenes.visual: The yellow dots drift out of the cadherin joints and out of frame. The BLUE beaded rods sag and wobble like loose strings; their tips slip apart in the middle of the gap. The 'arms outside' box turns RED. The GOLD pulse that was travelling stops at the gap; the TEAL and GREEN links on both sides stay intact, and the GOLD pulse no longer crosses the gap. On 'the sheet comes apart', zoom back out to the whole world: the row of cells rounds up and separates, exactly as in the hook. Then the yellow dots stream back, the cells knit again, and the arms stiffen, ready for the next scene.

scenes.tts: Now look down, at the matrix, the material cells secrete around themselves. Here the receptor is an integrin, a pair of subunits, alpha and beta. It grips a matrix protein, fibronectin, at a short tag, R G D.
scenes.narration: Now look down, at the matrix, the material cells secrete around themselves. Here the receptor is an integrin, a pair of subunits, α and β. It grips a matrix protein, fibronectin, at a short tag, RGD.
scenes.caption: Now look down, at the matrix, the material cells secrete around themselves. Here the receptor is an integrin, a pair of subunits, α and β. It grips a matrix protein, fibronectin, at a short tag, RGD.
scenes.visual: Camera tilts down along one cell to its base, where the GREY membrane meets the ORANGE matrix; the matrix fills the bottom half of the frame, its ropes gently swaying. Label 'matrix' in ORANGE. A PURPLE integrin, two lobes side by side labelled 'α' and 'β', rises into the membrane. On 'fibronectin', a thin ORANGE strand drifts up from the matrix; a small bright ORANGE patch on it is labelled 'RGD'. On 'R G D', the integrin stands extended with its head open and binds the RGD patch with a small flash (never draw or label the head as closing). Label 'integrin' in PURPLE. Labelled blocks only, no structures.

scenes.tts: Inside, talin ties the integrin's tail to actin, and vinculin adds extra ties to the same cable. Notice the pattern. The receptor has changed, but the four links have not. When the cell tugs on its cable, the pull runs down into the matrix.
scenes.narration: Inside, talin ties the integrin's tail to actin, and vinculin adds extra ties to the same cable. Notice the pattern. The receptor has changed, but the four links have not. When the cell tugs on its cable, the pull runs down into the matrix.
scenes.caption: Inside, talin ties the integrin's tail to actin, and vinculin adds extra ties to the same cable. Notice the pattern. The receptor has changed, but the four links have not. When the cell tugs on its cable, the pull runs down into the matrix.
scenes.visual: Inside the cell above the integrin, a long TEAL bar labelled 'talin' snaps onto the integrin's tail and reaches up to a GREEN actin cable, which docks onto it: one direct connection. Then two small TEAL blocks labelled 'vinculin' bind along the talin bar and each sends an extra short tie up to the same GREEN cable, as branches beside talin, not as a block in series. On 'Notice the pattern', the four numbered white tags from the adherens chain slide down and re-attach to the new links: '1 partner outside' on fibronectin, '2 receptor' on the integrin, '3 adaptors' on talin and vinculin, '4 cable' on actin; the adherens chain above briefly glows with its own four tags for comparison. On 'tugs', the GREEN cable contracts slightly and a GOLD pulse runs down the cable, through TEAL and PURPLE, into the ORANGE fibronectin strand, which straightens. Small label 'focal adhesion (cultured cells)' at the side.

scenes.tts: Two more junctions build the same chain with a different cable. Desmosomes join cell to cell. Hemidesmosomes pin a cell to the basement membrane, the thin matrix sheet beneath. In epithelia, both end on keratin, an intermediate filament, not on actin.
scenes.narration: Two more junctions build the same chain with a different cable. Desmosomes join cell to cell. Hemidesmosomes pin a cell to the basement membrane, the thin matrix sheet beneath. In epithelia, both end on keratin, an intermediate filament, not on actin.
scenes.caption: Two more junctions build the same chain with a different cable. Desmosomes join cell to cell. Hemidesmosomes pin a cell to the basement membrane, the thin matrix sheet beneath. In epithelia, both end on keratin, an intermediate filament, not on actin.
scenes.visual: The camera pulls back to show the base of two neighbouring cells and the ORANGE basement membrane sheet beneath them (label 'basement membrane'). On 'Desmosomes', a second junction appears lower down the side wall between the two cells: the same four-link chain shape, but its cable is PINK (label 'desmosome'). On 'Hemidesmosomes', a third chain appears at the base of one cell, running from the ORANGE sheet through a PURPLE receptor and TEAL adaptor to a PINK cable (label 'hemidesmosome'). On 'keratin, not actin', both PINK cables brighten and a label 'keratin cable' appears in PINK beside them, while the GREEN actin cable of the integrin chain dims for contrast.

scenes.tts: At the chain's far end is the matrix itself. Its collagen ropes straighten under a pull and resist it strongly. But squeeze the tissue, and the ropes buckle and go slack. Ropes are poor at pushing.
scenes.narration: At the chain's far end is the matrix itself. Its collagen ropes straighten under a pull and resist it strongly. But squeeze the tissue, and the ropes buckle and go slack. Ropes are poor at pushing.
scenes.caption: At the chain's far end is the matrix itself. Its collagen ropes straighten under a pull and resist it strongly. But squeeze the tissue, and the ropes buckle and go slack. Ropes are poor at pushing.
scenes.visual: Camera follows the ORANGE matrix downward until the wavy ORANGE ropes fill the frame (label 'collagen ropes'). On 'straighten under a pull', two GOLD arrows pull the tissue outward left and right; the wavy ropes straighten into taut lines and stop the stretch. On 'squeeze', the GOLD arrows flip to point inward from top and bottom; the ropes buckle and go slack and the tissue flattens, resisting only a little (reduced, not zero, resistance). On 'Ropes are poor at pushing', a white label 'strong in pulling, weak in squeezing' appears.

scenes.tts: So the matrix also holds a gel of proteoglycans, proteins with long sugar chains. In a first picture, the chains' negative charges draw in water, and the gel swells. Squeeze it, and it pushes back.
scenes.narration: So the matrix also holds a gel of proteoglycans, proteins with long sugar chains. In a first picture, the chains' negative charges draw in water, and the gel swells. Squeeze it, and it pushes back.
scenes.caption: So the matrix also holds a gel of proteoglycans, proteins with long sugar chains. In a first picture, the chains' negative charges draw in water, and the gel swells. Squeeze it, and it pushes back.
scenes.visual: Between the slack ropes, a pale orange gel fills in (label 'proteoglycan gel'). Zoom on one bottle-brush shape: a short core with many long bristles, each bristle studded with white minus signs. On 'draw in water', small light-blue water dots flow in from the edges among the bristles and the gel visibly swells (schematic). On 'Squeeze it', the inward GOLD arrows press again; the gel compresses a little, the minus signs crowd together, and the gel pushes the arrows back out. Corner label 'schematic'. Do not draw positive ions clustering on the chains.

scenes.tts: The tissue is one web of chains, from matrix ropes to cell cables. A real junction holds many chains side by side, sharing the load. One question is left. Does the pull change the links themselves?
scenes.narration: The tissue is one web of chains, from matrix ropes to cell cables. A real junction holds many chains side by side, sharing the load. One question is left. Does the pull change the links themselves?
scenes.caption: The tissue is one web of chains, from matrix ropes to cell cables. A real junction holds many chains side by side, sharing the load. One question is left. Does the pull change the links themselves?
scenes.visual: As the scene starts, zoom all the way out to the full world from the hook: the row of cells, the basement membrane, the matrix of ropes and gel. Every chain shown in the film lights up at once in its colours (BLUE cadherin chains between cells, PURPLE integrin chains and PINK hemidesmosome chains at the base), joined into one web. On 'many chains side by side', zoom briefly on one junction where several parallel chains glow together and the GOLD pulse splits among them. A GOLD pulse then spreads through the whole web, cell to cell and down into the matrix. On 'One question is left', the web dims slightly and the white question 'Does the pull change the links?' appears at the top and stays, unanswered; the gold pulse keeps travelling slowly.
End card: the take-home line in white over the dimmed world, with one adherens chain glowing in its four colours (BLUE, TEAL, GREEN, with YELLOW calcium) beneath it.
scenes.line: Each grip is a chain, outside partner to inside cable.
